payload.executive_summary: Candidate B1B delivers a Markdown-to-static-site generator as a monolithic CLI (O1) using thin-slice milestones. Milestone 1 produces a working CLI that ingests a folder of .md files and outputs bare HTML pages with preserved formatting (R1–R4, R11, R22). Milestone 2 adds forward-link detection, backlink computation, and backlink section rendering (R9, R10, R21). Milestone 3 introduces tag extraction and per-tag navigation pages (R7, R8, R20). Milestone 4 delivers client-side search index generation and search UI (R5, R19). Milestone 5 polishes the tool with error reporting (R12), cross-browser validation (R13), watch mode (R25), and optional features (R24, R26–R29). Blocking questions Q1 (link syntax) and Q2 (tag format) must be resolved before coding begins. XSS mitigation (K3) is enforced from day one by disabling raw HTML and blocking unsafe URL schemes. High HITL strictness ensures stakeholder sign-off at each milestone gate. This branch optimises for speed-to-first-value and simplicity at the cost of long-term extensibility.

architecture_choice.rationale: The monolithic single-command CLI (O1) minimises upfront design overhead, avoids plugin-API or SSG-dependency risks, and delivers the fastest path to a working end-to-end prototype. All build stages run in-memory in a single process, simplifying debugging and deployment. Thin-slice milestones let each core goal (G1–G5) be validated incrementally. The trade-off is reduced long-term extensibility compared to O2 or O3, but this is acceptable given the project's scope and the explicit deferral of COULD requirements to post-MVP.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: User invokes CLI (C1) with input/output paths → C2 recursively discovers .md files, parses Markdown to AST, extracts frontmatter/tags/links → C3 builds forward-link graph and computes backlinks → C4 aggregates tags into per-tag indexes → C5 builds client-side search index → C6 renders HTML pages (injecting backlinks, tags, navigation) and writes static assets to output directory → C7 (client-side JS) loads search index in browser and provides search UI.

decision_log.question: Which architecture option to use?
decision_log.rationale: Minimises upfront design overhead and delivers the fastest path to a working end-to-end prototype. All stages run in-memory in a single process, simplifying debugging and deployment. Thin-slice milestones validate each goal incrementally.
alternatives_considered: O2 — Custom plugin-based SSG core: higher extensibility but significant upfront API design cost and over-engineering risk for initial scope.
O3 — Eleventy-based: reduces custom code but introduces SSG dependency constraints and upgrade risks.
O4 — Multi-tool pipeline: high modularity but complex orchestration UX and intermediate schema maintenance.
what_would_change_this_decision: Requirement for third-party theme/plugin ecosystem support.
Need to support multiple search backends or renderers simultaneously.
Scale exceeding thousands of notes where SSG incremental builds (O3) would provide significant performance advantage.

decision_log.question: What milestone strategy to follow?
decision_log.choice: Thin-slice: each milestone delivers a shippable, testable increment covering a distinct core goal.
decision_log.rationale: Thin slices allow early validation of each goal (G1–G5) against its acceptance tests before proceeding, reducing integration risk and enabling early feedback.
alternatives_considered: Layer-cake: build all backend components first, then UI — delays end-to-end validation.
Big-bang: single milestone with all features — high integration risk and late feedback.
what_would_change_this_decision: Strong coupling between features that prevents independent slicing.
Stakeholder preference for a single comprehensive delivery.

decision_log.question: When to resolve blocking questions Q1 (link syntax) and Q2 (tag format)?
decision_log.choice: Resolve both before any coding begins (pre-M1 gate).
decision_log.rationale: Q1 and Q2 are blocking; link syntax affects C2, C3, and C6, while tag format affects C2 and C4. Deferring them would cause rework across multiple components. Alignment warnings AL-001 and AL-002 flag these as blockers.
alternatives_considered: Defer Q1 to M2 and Q2 to M3 — risks rework in M1 parser if conventions change.
Support all formats from the start — increases complexity and testing surface without clear user need.
what_would_change_this_decision: User explicitly requests multi-format support from day one.
A clear industry-standard convention emerges that eliminates ambiguity.

evidence_pointers.note: AL-001 and AL-002 flag Q1/Q2 as blockers

decision_log.question: How to mitigate XSS risk (K3) in the Markdown renderer?
decision_log.choice: Disable raw HTML passthrough and block unsafe URL schemes (javascript:, data:, vbscript:) from day one in C2/C6.
decision_log.rationale: K3 is critical severity. Enabling raw HTML by default exposes site readers to injection attacks. Disabling it is the safest default; an explicit opt-in configuration can be added later with documented risk.
alternatives_considered: Allow raw HTML with sanitization library — adds dependency and residual risk.
Allow raw HTML by default — unacceptable given critical severity.
what_would_change_this_decision: User explicitly requires raw HTML embedding and accepts the risk with sign-off.
A proven, well-maintained HTML sanitizer is adopted with comprehensive test coverage.

decision_log.question: How to handle path traversal risk (K9) during ingestion?
decision_log.choice: Constrain ingestion to the declared root directory in C2; reject symlinks by default; reject paths escaping the root.
decision_log.rationale: K9 is high severity. Following symlinks or allowing path escape could leak local files into the generated site. Rejecting symlinks is the safe default.
alternatives_considered: Follow symlinks with user confirmation — adds complexity and residual risk.
No restriction — unacceptable given high severity.
what_would_change_this_decision: User workflow requires symlinked note directories and explicitly opts in.

decision_log.question: When to address search index scalability (K4)?
decision_log.choice: Defer concrete benchmarking to M4 with a defined performance budget step; apply basic index-size controls (stemming, stop words) from the start.
decision_log.rationale: Search is delivered in M4. Benchmarking earlier would be premature since the index generator (C5) is not built until M4. Basic controls are low-cost to include from the start.
alternatives_considered: Benchmark in M1 — premature, no search component exists yet.
Ignore until post-MVP — unacceptable given high severity of K4.
what_would_change_this_decision: User confirms a very large corpus (10k+ notes) requiring chunked/sharded indexing from the start.
Performance targets defined earlier via Q3 resolution.

decision_log.question: How to handle COULD-priority features (R26–R29)?
decision_log.choice: Explicitly defer to post-M5; only implement with product approval to avoid scope creep (K20).
decision_log.rationale: K20 identifies scope creep risk. COULD features are not required for core goals. Deferring them keeps the team focused on MUST and SHOULD requirements through M5.
alternatives_considered: Include in M5 unconditionally — risks delaying core polish work.
Drop entirely — removes optionality for stakeholders.
what_would_change_this_decision: Stakeholder explicitly prioritises a COULD feature above a SHOULD feature.
Remaining M5 effort is minimal and team has capacity.

supplemental_evaluations.title: Security Posture Assessment
supplemental_evaluations.notes: K3 (XSS, critical) is mitigated from M1 by disabling raw HTML and blocking unsafe URL schemes. K9 (path traversal, high) is mitigated from M1 by constraining ingestion to the declared root and rejecting symlinks. Both mitigations are verified by dedicated test suites included in M1 deliverables. The acceptance strategy notes that a security-focused XSS acceptance test must be added before M1 exits; this is captured as DL4.

evidence.note: Critical XSS risk with planned mitigation
High path traversal risk with planned mitigation

supplemental_evaluations.title: Blocking Questions Gate
supplemental_evaluations.notes: Q1 (internal link syntax) and Q2 (tag format) are both high-impact, blocking questions. This candidate requires both to be resolved and documented before M1 work begins. If they remain unresolved, the HITL policy mandates interruption. The branch risk posture explicitly prioritises resolving these first.

The acceptance strategy also calls for a security-focused XSS test (not yet a canonical AT) before M1 exit — this is tracked as DL4 and flagged in W1.
